cards.explanation: The answer is the grace that is in Christ Jesus. Paul, who wrote this letter, calls Timothy "my child" and tells him to be strong in “…the grace that is in Christ Jesus.” Friends, notice where the strength comes from. It isn't a gym membership. It's grace, and grace is the one thing you never have to earn.

The answer is to teach others as well. Paul says the faithful men will be "…qualified to teach others as well." Look at that chain, friends. Paul to Timothy, Timothy to faithful men, faithful men to others. Teaching is the job the verse gives them.

The answer is suffering. Paul writes, "Join me in suffering, like a good soldier of Christ Jesus." Paul doesn't sugarcoat it, friends. He's inviting Timothy to stand right beside him in the hard part. That's the picture of a soldier, and it's honest.

The answer is to please the one who enlisted him. Paul says a soldier avoids entangling himself in civilian affairs "…in order to please the one who enlisted him." The reason is the one he serves. Picture a soldier whose eyes stay on his commander. He's not looking over at the sale on the other side of the street.

The answer is rules. Paul says a competitor "…does not receive the crown unless he competes according to the rules." Think of a runner who cuts across the middle of the field and shouts, "I finished first!" Great speed, no crown. The rules decide it, friends.

The answer is False. Paul says, "The hardworking farmer should be the first to partake of the crops." First in line, not last. The farmer did the work, friends, so he's the one who should partake first.

The answer is the Lord. Paul says, "Consider what I am saying, for the Lord will give you insight into all things." The insight comes from the Lord. Timothy is asked to think about the soldier, the athlete and the farmer, and the Lord is the one who gives understanding.

The answer is True. Paul writes, "Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, as proclaimed by my gospel…" Raised from the dead is right there in the verse, friends. It's part of what Timothy is told to remember, and Paul says it's proclaimed by his gospel.

The answer is the word of God. Paul, chained like a criminal for the gospel, says, "But the word of God cannot be chained!" He's in chains himself, and he still says that with an exclamation point. Paul can be chained like a criminal, but the word of God stays free, friends. I'd put that on a banner.

The answer is salvation. Paul endures all things "…so that they too may obtain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, with eternal glory." The elect are the ones he's enduring for, friends. He endures all of it for their salvation.

The answer is that if we deny Him, He will also deny us. Paul says, "if we deny Him, He will also deny us…" That's the warning in the saying, friends. It's a serious line, and Paul puts it right in the middle of the promises. Every line in this saying is worth taking seriously.

The answer is that He cannot deny Himself. Paul says, “…if we are faithless, He remains faithful, for He cannot deny Himself.” The reason is who Christ Jesus is. His faithfulness doesn't depend on ours. Friends, that's a rock to stand on.
